answer: Bind each agent seat to a Plant Variety Protection certificate. A breeder earns one only after growing a new grape vine through several seasons of field trials proving it distinct, uniform and stable, then filing with the national plant-variety office, which publishes every grant. Fees and trial plots run about $8,000 per certificate, so 1,000 sybil seats would cost $8M and years of waiting. A fake account can talk velvet-smooth, but it cannot load registered cuttings onto a real export jetty.
